dossier.valuation_method: Probability-weighted, time-discounted scenario valuation (rNPV) of MST adoption outcomes over a built-up net-cash + weak-IP floor; success-case equity values derived from a transparent royalty-ramp DCF and cross-checked vs mature semi-IP royalty multiples (Arm/Rambus/CEVA); probabilities anchored by a correlation-adjusted TRL-gate funnel and an outside view of historical materials insertions; 16% systematic+illiquidity discount rate
dossier.thesis_summary: Atomera is a pre-revenue (~$65k FY2025 revenue) semiconductor materials-IP licensor burning ~$15-17M/yr; its value is the probability-weighted PV of a future royalty stream IF its MST film is adopted into high-volume manufacturing, over a ~$1.00/share net-cash floor. The science is real and peer-reviewed with many shots on goal (GAA diffusion-blocking, DRAM, RF-SOI, GaN), but after 10 years public it has zero royalty revenue, its flagship STMicro license just failed at qualification (Oct 2025), and it is structurally a no-fab licensing play of the kind (SuVolta/Amberwave) that historically struggled even with good science. A correlation-adjusted TRL-gate funnel yields ~30% odds of any production conversion and ~15% of a high-volume win, producing an FMV near $1.80/share — overwhelmingly option value in a convex payoff, and far below the ~$7.6 market price / ~$10 street target, which embed an implied success probability ~2.5-3x what the record supports.
key_value_drivers: Probability MST converts to a royalty-bearing HVM license (correlation-adjusted funnel: ~30% any / ~15% high-volume / ~5% blockbuster)
Royalty run-rate per socket ($50-80M/yr one socket; $250-350M/yr multi-socket) at near-100% incremental margin, NOL-shielded, corroborated by third-party wafer/ASP data
Time-to-first-royalty (3.5-4.5 yrs) and the 16% systematic+illiquidity discount rate on distant payoffs
Ongoing equity dilution modeled from the burn (~46-47M shares in success, ~52-53M in failure; authorized share count rising to 95M)
Equipment-OEM (likely Applied Materials) co-marketing channel into the four GAA customers, which also gates takeout optionality
key_risks: Modal (~70%) outcome is non-conversion plus slow, price-dilutive equity raises
Reliability/qualification failures (as with STMicro BCD110, Oct 2025) recur at the decisive gate
No fab and no leverage; the no-fab licensing insertion model has a poor historical record (SuVolta, Amberwave)
MST thermal-budget and mid-line integration constraints narrow addressable flows
Active securities-law investigation; single-technology, key-person concentration
Market price (~$7.6) embeds an implied success probability ~2.5-3x the evidence — large downside to intrinsic value
what_would_change_my_mind: A signed HVM license with a named Tier-1 customer (not a JDA/evaluation)
An RF-SOI or GaN 'starting-wafer' customer converting to production royalties
Equipment-OEM partner committing reactor co-development with a volume customer (also raises takeout odds)
Conversely: another flagship engagement collapsing at qualification or an accelerated discounted raise

judge_gaps: A formal Monte Carlo over the joint probability/value distribution would replace the four-point discrete scenarios with a continuous expected value and explicit confidence intervals (polish, not a flaw).
Could model the near-term catalyst path — how fast and how far FV converges toward the market if a named HVM license is signed in 2026 — to size the asymmetry for anyone considering the short side.
Uses a ~38M fully-diluted estimate; pulling the exact option/RSU/PSU overhang from the proxy would tighten the per-share denominators slightly.
Insider ownership and the relative-TSR PSU incentive structure are noted only briefly; a short paragraph on management alignment and any insider selling would round out the governance picture.
